newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria to end gas flaring by 2010 - oil minister.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria to end gas flaring by 2010 - oil minister.

text.p: Nigeria has set a deadline of 2010 to halt the flaring of gas in order to curb environmental pollution, oil minister Dan Etete said.
Etete announced this on Wednesday at an oil seminar in the midwestern town of Warri.
"About 80 percent of the natural gas produced in the country is being flared and our country has been labelled with a worldwide notoriety as a result," he said.
The target would be achieved through many gas-related projects on the drawing board, the oil minister said.
Among these are the liquefied natural gas plant being built in Bonny, southeastern Nigeria at a cost of $4 billion, Africa's biggest project.
Another project is to supply gas to West African countries while a gas gathering project involving Chevron Corp's Nigerian subsidiary at Escravos is also being undertaken.
Nigeria has more gas reserves than crude oil but policy changes and a high turnover of executives in the petroleum ministry has stalled many gas projects.
The deadline set to stop gas flaring coincides with an economic programme tagged "Vision 2010" launched last week by military ruler General Sani Abacha to turn Nigeria into an industrial giant.
